description:
FILED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5 (run/ CHECK 1 + CHECK 2).

perl reads its own `#!` line and applies the switches on it (perlrun: "the #!
line is always examined for switches").  That is how these test files work at
all: they carry `#!./perl -n`, `#!./perl -na`, `#!./perl -anFx+`,
`#!./perl -IFoo::Bar -IBla`.  PCL ignores the line entirely, so the body runs
ONCE as a plain program with `$_` undef instead of inside the implicit
`while (<>)` loop.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL HEAD).  /tmp/sb.pl:
    #!/usr/bin/perl -n
    print "[$_]";
    __END__
  perl /tmp/sb.pl </dev/null                -> nothing (the loop reads stdin)
  printf 'a\nb\n' | perl /tmp/sb.pl         -> [a
                                               ][b
                                               ]
  printf 'a\nb\n' | ./runpcl /tmp/sb.pl     -> [] -- the body ran once

ROWS BEHIND IT (measured s473t5d, `--jobs 1`):
  run/switchn.t     3 fail + 1 short   #!./perl -n
  run/switcha.t     2 fail + 1 short   #!./perl -na
  run/switchF.t     2 fail + 1 short   #!./perl -anFx+
  run/switchp.t     2 fail + 2 short   #!./perl -p
  run/switch0.t     1 fail             #!./perl -0
  run/switchx.t     9 fail + 5 short   #!./perl -x (plus -x's own diagnostics)
  run/switchI.t     2 of 4 fail        #!./perl -IFoo::Bar -IBla
  run/noswitch.t    1 fail             (its `*ARGV = *DATA` + no switch)
  run/switches.t    ~30 of its rows are the `... on #! line` family
                    ("Can't emulate -x on #! line", -E/-S/-V/-e/-f, and
                     "Spaces on the #! line")

FIX SHAPE (rule 11 -- the machinery exists twice over): the whole switch
REWRITING for -n/-p/-a/-F/-l/-0/-x is already written, in
`tools/pclperl-for-tests` (its "Switch semantics that perl implements by
rewriting the program: do the same" block).  The right home is `pl2cl` itself:
read the `#!` line of the SOURCE and apply the switches there, so `pcl`,
`./runpcl`, `tools/run-perl-suite.pl` and the sweep all get it from one place.
Doing it in the RUNNERS instead would be a third copy.

Probe the case it would BREAK first: a `#!` line naming a switch PCL does not
implement must not change the program (perl warns "Can't emulate -X on #!
line" and exits 255 for some of them -- run/switches.t asserts exactly that
text for -x/-E/-S/-V), and a shebang without `perl` in it is not examined at
all.

Table: docs/pcl-commands.md; what differs: docs/not-supported.md "Perl's command-line switches".  -n -p -a -F -l -0 -g -i -s -x -S -E -I -M -m -c -w -C implemented; -T/-t run + announced; -W -X -U -f inert; -D perl's message; -d -u refused; -v = version, -V/-V:name from %Config, -h/-?; a script's #! line honoured (#1702).  Guards: Pl/t/pcl-switches-01.t (122 rows), tools/t/harness-switches.t rows 5-11, Pl/t/script-cache-01.t (+5).  One-liner battery 147 of 152 (ol-052 #2665, ol-062/064 #2664, ol-161/164 smartmatch). subject: a script's OWN `#!perl -SWITCHES` line is not honoured: perl re-parses its shebang and applies the switches it finds, PCL ignores them -- 8 companion files
